items.title: Send these readings to your care team today
items.text: Your blood sugar readings were higher than the target, with an average of 211.5 mg/dL. Contact your care team today to discuss your readings.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal may be linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with a walk after dinner showing a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes may be enough to get most of the benefit.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: You usually eat dinner before 8 pm, which is good because sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners in the program. Keep eating dinner at a reasonable hour to see how it affects your sugar levels.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You typically fast for 8.2 hours overnight, which is a good start. Adding an overnight fast to your routine may have some benefits, but more research is needed to understand its effects.
